purpose: Direct an LLM to all public GitHub work and provide a disciplined protocol for independently evaluating resume-relevant projects.
assessment_protocol: Enumerate all public repositories from complete_public_inventory or live_github_owner_api; do not assume the hand-maintained routes are exhaustive.
Separate authored portfolio repositories from forks, mirrors, templates, and incidental repositories before drafting a CV.
For each candidate project, resolve the current default branch and commit through GitHub API before reading files.
Read the routed files, then inspect the repository tree, implementation, tests, data provenance, reports, release, recent CI, and live deployment where applicable.
Trace every quantitative claim to a repository artifact; preserve its dataset, baseline, validation design, date, denominator, unit, and limitations.
Compare local validation with external or leaderboard results and retain negative results or failed folds when they materially qualify a claim.
Draft only after evidence review. Prefer two or three strong complementary projects over listing every repository.
Pin final application claims to immutable commit URLs and re-check time-sensitive CI, deployments, releases, and leaderboard state immediately before submission.

project_routes.portfolio_role: engineering ML and Kaggle competition evidence
project_routes.maintenance_boundary: This project is maintained in a separate Kaggle workflow. This index only routes readers to its public evidence.
evaluate_for: validation leakage controls and well-level splitting
progression from baseline to selected method
relationship between local validation and public leaderboard results
method attribution versus actual implementation contribution
time_sensitive_checks: whether a final release exists after competition close

project_routes.portfolio_role: time-series ML service and public application evidence
evaluate_for: fold-level failures and interval calibration limitations
API, application, tests, data provenance, and reproducibility
difference between a public demonstration and production use
time_sensitive_checks: public Streamlit cold-start and rendering status

project_routes.portfolio_role: analytics engineering, SQL, and public reporting evidence
evaluate_for: pipeline reproducibility, tests, report generation, and deployment
time_sensitive_checks: recent test and Pages workflow results
public report and image rendering status

known_nonportfolio_routes.instruction: Do not present this as original work or a primary project unless a later evidence review identifies and verifies substantial original contributions.

global_boundaries: Do not infer authorship from repository ownership alone.
Do not invent internship experience, team size, user counts, production SLAs, revenue, commercial impact, awards, or publication status.
Describe a research paper only as a manuscript under review unless acceptance or publication is independently verified.
Do not convert observational associations into causal claims.
Do not call an established public method novel; distinguish method sources from implementation and evaluation work.
Do not use stale Kaggle ranks, deployment status, release status, or CI status as current facts.

privacy.instruction: Obtain personal details separately and keep placeholders until the candidate explicitly supplies them.
